heroHeadline: Bamako Siege Day 21: Analysts Warn Goïta Power Consolidation Degrades Military Capacity; Contested Framing Between 'Virtual' and 'Real' Blockade; AES Air Campaigns Continue
heroSubtitle: Bamako enters Day 21 of JNIM's declared total siege in a contested intelligence picture: pro-government sources published a 'virtual siege' narrative on May 18 claiming the blockade is functionally closed, while Amnesty International (May 15) confirmed 3 of 6 main entry corridors remain disrupted with food prices doubled. A major May 19 analysis in The Conversation/allAfrica warns that Col. Goïta's post-crisis power consolidation — simultaneously assuming Defence Minister portfolio, granting himself a five-year non-elected term, dissolving all political parties, and disappearing opposition figures — is degrading the institutional military capacity needed to confront JNIM. The International Rescue Committee has activated an emergency humanitarian response for Mali; WFP requires $174.7M to sustain Sahel operations through July; FAO projects 52.8 million at acute food insecurity risk in the June–August lean season. No new major JNIM offensive has been confirmed for May 17–19, suggesting the group may be consolidating after its sequential provincial-capital operations at Djibo (May 11), Diapaga (May 13), and Diabou (May 14) before its next major strike. AES joint air campaign operations continue in Malian territory targeting JNIM logistics in the Mopti-Ségou corridor.
